places.name: Bogmother Causeway

places.name: Tearmouth

why.founding: Where the north river meets navigable water, cargo has to change hulls. A two-culture port grew at the transfer point: Argonian on the water, Dunmer on the bank. Each half calls itself the port.
why.siteAdvantages: The head of deep-draught navigation. Below it a keeled hull can float. Above it, shallow craft only. Two dredging schemes have failed to move the line.
why.occupantsMotive: Transfer fees and warehousing. A customs presence run out of Thorn with two clerks. A great deal of business the two clerks are not shown.
why.pressures: Both halves of the town want the customs house on the other side of the water; the Thorn road wants a bridge; and the whole place empties for six weeks when the river runs too hard to transfer at all.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose half its trade to a deeper channel and all of it to a bridge. It has resisted both for a century.

places.name: Ten-Maur-Wolk
aliases: Tenmar Wall (the Imperial exonym; the Third Empire's maps renamed the site)

why.founding: A temple to Boethiah and Vaermina raised by Dunmer dissidents who fled the Tribunal, then abandoned by them. The Third Empire's surveyors renamed it Tenmar Wall on their maps. The north kept the old name. The market that carries the shortened form grew half a morning's walk away, on the road, which is as close as anyone wanted to build.
why.siteAdvantages: Off the road, in a hollow the tracks curve around. Every carter in the north can point at the hollow from the bend.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The marker posts around it are maintained.
why.pressures: The market town that borrowed its name lives off the road and pretends the ruin is somebody else's business; the second atrocity on this ground is the Dres slave road that ran past the district, not anything the dissidents built.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would draw a cult within a year if the markers ever stopped being renewed.

places.name: Ten-Thousand-Nests

why.founding: A stand of dead trees in shallow water where the north's wading birds nest in numbers that make the stand uninhabitable and the ground beneath it the richest fertiliser source in the region.
why.siteAdvantages: Dead standing timber over water. No predator route in. Forty years of guano under it.
why.occupantsMotive: The villages take guano for the terraces in one licensed month and stay away for eleven, an arrangement enforced by the smell as much as by anyone.
why.pressures: The saltrice growers want more than one month; the villages that eat the eggs want none at all; the stand itself is rotting and falling tree by tree.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would relocate entirely if the stand came down. Birds do. Nobody knows where to.

places.name: Zuuk

why.founding: A Kothringi settlement that died in 2E 561, one year into the Flu, with its founder's name still on it.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm bank on the Shadowfen channels. Good ground. Every boat that passes sees it standing empty.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. The neighbouring villages route boats past without stopping. They have done for three hundred years.
why.pressures: It is the best unclaimed landing in the district. What keeps it unclaimed is the taboo.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be resettled within a decade if the north ever grew enough to need the ground.

vibe.silhouette: A stone landing with a name cut into it. Behind it a settlement whose walls stand and whose roofs do not.
vibe.palette: Silver-grey stone, black doorways and a green that has grown to the doorsteps and stopped.
vibe.materials: Kothringi coursed stone, finer than anything around it; not one Argonian repair anywhere.
vibe.signatureFeature: The name at the landing: the founder's, still legible and uneffaced.
vibe.condition: Untouched. Nothing has been taken, which after three centuries is remarkable.
vibe.mood: Still, reproachful, oddly intact.
vibe.approach: From the channel you see the landing steps first. The name is cut at eye height from a boat.
vibe.senses: Water on stone steps; wind through roofless rooms; no boats stopping.

questHooks.opportunity: kothringi work stands on the best ground on the road; every villager gives a different reason for leaving it
